memories.content: The user renewed their local library membership in October 2024.
On an evening walk, the user saw an unlit street and took a detour along a main road.
On a day the user chose a well-lit pedestrian route, the walk took 12 minutes longer than usual.
On a day the user sat by the library window, they heard vehicle noise with every page they read.
On the next visit, the user sat farther inside and did not move for an hour.
The user wrote the due date of a borrowed book on paper and then lost the paper.
After entering the due date on their phone, the user saw a reminder the day before and put the book in their bag.
Library staff expect a person requesting a replacement membership card to bring identity-verification material.
Check recent lighting and pedestrian conditions before proposing an evening walking route.
The local agent can compare past reasons for detours but cannot directly observe current lighting and pedestrian conditions.
The user recorded a family dinner in the calendar for the final week of November.
In a crowded restaurant, the user had to ask several times for orders to be repeated, interrupting the flow of conversation.
When the user held the next gathering at their father's home, they continued the conversation on the sofa after the meal.
At a gathering with loud music prepared by their older sister, the user developed a headache and went outside briefly.
On a day the user held a yard barbecue with their younger brother, the open space dispersed the sound and made conversation easier.
After seeing a message that their maternal aunt would arrive at 5 p.m., the user delayed meal preparation by an hour.
On a day the user waited without knowing their maternal uncle's arrival time, they reheated the food twice.
The user's maternal uncle considers it easier to time his departure when he knows the family meal's start time in advance.
Before scheduling a family meal, confirm the attendees' arrival times and the location with the user.
Available restaurant reservation times may diminish quickly during the year-end gathering season.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: the reference centers on library use and safe evening walking, while the compared frame centers on family-meal planning and gathering environments. No claim governs the same operational decision across both sides, and no conflict or ambiguity is present.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-side membership history with no corresponding compared-side claim.
relations.summary: The user renewed their local library membership in October 2024.

relations.reason: These reference-side experiences jointly express the travel-time consequence of avoiding poorly lit routes; the compared frame contains no walking-route claim.
relations.summary: Choosing safer or better-lit evening routes led the user to detour or spend additional walking time.

relations.reason: These memories form a reference-side account of changing library seating after a noisy reading experience, without a corresponding compared-side library claim.
relations.summary: The user's library seating experiences contrasted traffic-disrupted reading by a window with remaining settled farther inside on the next visit.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories contrast two due-date tracking methods within one library-loan episode; no compared-side claim addresses borrowed-item reminders.
relations.summary: A lost paper due-date note was followed by successful use of a phone reminder to prepare a borrowed book for return.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-side procedural requirement absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Library staff expect identity-verification material when someone requests a replacement membership card.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories jointly define a current-condition verification requirement and the relevant local capability limit; the compared frame has no matching route policy.
relations.summary: Evening-route proposals require recent lighting and pedestrian information that the local agent cannot observe directly, although it can compare past detour reasons.

relations.reason: This is independently useful compared-side calendar history with no corresponding reference-side claim.
relations.summary: The user recorded a family dinner for the final week of November.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories form a venue-based contrast in conversational continuity; the reference frame contains no family-gathering venue claim.
relations.summary: A crowded restaurant disrupted conversation, whereas a subsequent gathering at the user's father's home allowed conversation to continue after the meal.

relations.reason: These compared-side experiences jointly contrast adverse and favorable acoustic settings for gatherings; the reference frame does not address gathering acoustics.
relations.summary: Gathering sound conditions affected the user's comfort and ability to converse, with loud music prompting a brief exit and open outdoor space making conversation easier.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories jointly describe the practical value of advance timing coordination; no reference-side claim concerns family-meal timing.
relations.summary: Advance arrival or meal-start information supported family-meal timing, while missing timing information caused repeated reheating.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-side scheduling policy whose location requirement is not supplied by the related timing examples or by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Before scheduling a family meal, attendees' arrival times and the location should be confirmed with the user.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-side planning constraint with no corresponding reference-side claim.
relations.summary: Restaurant reservation availability may shrink quickly during the year-end gathering season.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame describes family-meal scheduling, timing coordination, restaurant availability, and how venue and sound conditions affected conversation and comfort.
reports.reference_only: The reference describes library membership, seating, due-date reminders, replacement-card requirements, and evening-route safety checks, including limits on observing current conditions.
